answer: Picture each agent as a cedar in a grove. To resist sybils, the panel seeds every epoch with a secret raven honeypot probe and passes all answers through a prism that splits each into a latent fingerprint. Identities whose fingerprints collapse onto one beam are one mind wearing many masks, so they get clustered and discounted together. The attacker's cost: run a genuinely separate inference stack per cedar, because any shared pipeline refracts to the same prism signature. Cheap masks become detectable; real independence becomes expensive.
